title: Same-key adaptive provider memoization
motivation: F-AHL28 confirmed one adaptive cache acquisition per physical advance and measured warm adaptive bind near 0.6 microseconds. F-AHL28A showed that removing only the support-array deep copy reduced bind cost by about 31 percent, below its frozen 50 percent retention gate, so that repair was reverted. Code authority shows the serialized backend also destroys and recreates the adaptive provider on every parameter configuration.

repair.provider_lifetime: retain the adaptive provider object across repeated serialized parameter configurations while adaptive_hydraulics_active remains true
repair.representation_identity: store the exact adaptive representation cache key in the provider
repair.same_key_rebind: rebind only the step-duration-dependent authoritative analytical fallback and current cofgen pointer; reuse the existing immutable provider-owned table without shared-cache acquisition
repair.different_key_rebind: use the existing exact-key shared cache and replace the provider-owned table only after successful acquisition
repair.adaptive_disabled: deallocate retained adaptive provider and preserve analytical default route

frozen_semantics: exact cache key equality, not fingerprint-only equality
same builder, support points, error tolerances and policy versions
same dry-tail C=1e-13 relevance floor and analytical fallback
same qbot and accepted-trajectory analytical fallbacks

qualification.cache_accounting: after first acquisition, repeated same-key provider binds must not increment shared-cache hits
qualification.reference_floor_timing: remeasure after all semantic gates pass

decision_rule: Retain the repair only if same-key warm bind falls by at least 75 percent from the frozen F-AHL28 baseline and all semantic/regression gates pass.
